_comment: Keyword topics for the guards (Scripts/guard_npc.gd, npc_conversation.gd). 'by_name' topics are checked before 'shared', so a guard can have their own answer for something; 'merchant_lines' are picked by where Sahren is right now. Directions use the whiteboard map: Lumora is north, the docks southwest, the graveyard west, goblins and bandits southeast, spiders far west by the sea. All lines are DRAFTS awaiting approval. {word} = clickable keyword.

lines: Lumora lies just beyond the gate, straight north: walls, markets, the Wardens. Show your coin, not your blade.
Lumora's north of us, through the gate. Mind your manners inside, and you'll find nothing but welcome.
The grey cat by the gate? Kenji. Bring him ten rat tails and he'll bless you for the trouble. Don't ask me why. I stopped asking.
Oni? The little tortoiseshell that patrols the road. She hunts rats. Kenji likes what she leaves behind.
Aldric the Provisioner and the Apothecary keep their stalls near the gate: food, water, torches, scrolls. Aldric's honest, if not cheap.

sequence: The docks are a long walk southwest, down along the coast. Sandcrest Landing, where the boats put in.
Harbour Master Tobias Sandcrest keeps the place. He'll sell you passage north, if there were a boat to take you.
The graveyard's west of the gate, a few minutes along the wall. Bones that don't lie still, and worse in the crypts.
Go by day, and not alone if you're green.

lines: Goblin camps sit far to the southeast, out past the signpost road. They don't fight fair, and they don't fight alone. Not a place for the green.
Bandits hold camps to the southeast, between the road and the goblins. They rob whoever walks alone. If you go, go strong.
The archery range is east of the gate, the straw targets along the far end. Guard Halric keeps the firing line. Mind where you stand.
Spiders nest far to the west, up along the cliffs by the sea. Webs across the path, and more of them than you'd like. Not a place to go alone.
Dustwalkers raid the roads. Folk in Lumora mistake them for the Djhanid, and that's an insult to the Djhanid. Learn the difference.
The Djhanid keep to the deep dunes and trust no one. They trouble nobody who leaves them be. Leave them be.
Poor souls lost to the sun, out in the deep dunes. Don't get close if you see one. They don't know you're not a shadow.
There's a campfire on the road south of the gate. Warmth for the weary, and a good place to cook what you kill.
The signpost stands well south along the road. Past it lies the Dustwind Plateaus, tougher country. Come back stronger.
Rats, snakes and scarabs near the gate. Worse further out. Stay near the road until you've a few levels behind you.
The sigil's with the Captain now. What comes of it isn't mine to say. Not yet.
The Weavemother, at the heart of the den, and whatever she's wearing that no spider should. Take friends. Bring it to me.

sequence: That silk was fed on something, and I don't like what. Somebody is keeping that den's mother alive, and making her worse.
The scouts told of a queen out there, a {Weavemother}. Kill her and bring me whatever she carries that a spider shouldn't. It's not a kill for one hunter. Take friends. Please.

lines: Six hanks of the grey silk the blighted spiders leave, from the den out west. Bring them to me.

sequence: The {spiders} in the den, far out west past the cliffs, have gone wrong. Scouts used to come back with bites and complaints. Lately they come back quiet.
I need proof, not stories. Bring me six hanks of the grey {silk} the blighted ones spin and bring them to me. You'll know it by the purple in it.

lines: Gate duty. Nobody gets through without one of us noticing. Well... mostly nobody.
Dessik Coinhand and the Lumoran strongbox. He'll be near the wreck, out along the south road. Bring it back to me.
The house has its strongbox and Dessik's dead. That's the wagon settled. Thank you again.

sequence: A Lumoran trading wagon was hit on the south road, long way out to the southwest. The driver never made it to us. What was in it, we can guess.
There's a brigand out that way who calls himself {Dessik} Coinhand. If you go, the wreck should have a note or two on it. Bring me back what he took.
That medal. Where did you... it says Halvek. Sergeant Halvek trained me.
He's the one on the graveyard road? Still... Give it to me, friend. It's time somebody let him stop.

lines: Sergeant Halvek was one of ours. Nobody's seen him in years. If he's walking the graveyard road as a corpse, I'd want to know, and I'd want his medal.

sequence: The graveyard lies west of the gate. A few minutes along the wall, and you'll feel it before you see it.
Skeletons by day, worse by night. And the mausoleum has something in it that doesn't stay dead. Don't go alone, and don't go green.

lines: I walk the road from the gate to the signpost and back. Anything that lives out there knows my boots.

sequence: Three goblin camps, far southeast. Ten to a camp, and they'll call for friends.
Take a group, or wait until you're a good few levels stronger. That's a sergeant's honest advice.
Bandits hold the ground between the road and the goblins. They're hunters of the lonely and the careless.
Their leaders hit hard. If you must go, go in numbers.
The range is mine. Straw targets at the far end, and the shooters stand behind this line.
Loose a few if you like. The wind takes the arrows of anyone who rushes.
The docks are a long walk southwest, along the coast. Sandcrest Landing.
The harbour master there sells tokens for the Bastion ferry, but the ship's a long way out. Don't expect a boat soon.

coming: A peddler's coming up the west road with a pack the size of a house. Sahren, the Djhanid. He always stops at the docks first.
Sahren's on the road, heading for the docks. You'll catch him there if you're quick.
dock: The Djhanid peddler, Sahren, is set up at the docks. He won't stay long. Go now.
Sahren's at the docks with his pack. He'll be along to the gate afterward, if you'd rather wait.
gate: Sahren's at the gate right now. The Djhanid peddler with the pack. Rare goods, or so he says.
The peddler's here! By the wall, near the gate. Take a look before he packs up.
gone: Sahren left already. Gone back to the sands. He'll be along again, though I couldn't say when.
none: A Djhanid peddler comes through now and then. Sahren, they call him. I couldn't give you a day.
